newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan police seize hundreds of Moslem militants.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan police seize hundreds of Moslem militants.

text.p: Police seized hundreds of Moslem militants in the Pakistan's populous Punjab province overnight to try to quell sectarian unrest, officials said.
They said the Punjab provincial government had ordered the crackdown, which began at midnight (1900 GMT Sunday), following a spate of killings involving rival religious groups.
In the latest attacks, gunmen on motorcycles killed at least five people, four of them in a mosque, in Lahore on Sunday.

The activists detained overnight included members of the Sunni Moslem Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) organisation and two Shi'ite Moslem groups, Sipah-i-Mohammad Pakistan (SMP) and Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan (TJP), officials and relatives said.
The Punjab provincial government said on Sunday it had decided to seize all literature fanning sectarian prejudices.

Sectarian violence is rife in Punjab, where militant Sunni and Shi'ite factions are engaged in a feud that officials say has killed more than 100 people so far this year, including religious scholars, lawyers and doctors.
